title: Aaron Swartz was prosecuted for scraping, while Meta does it without consequence
titleZh: 亚伦·斯沃茨 (Aaron Swartz) 因抄袭而被起诉，而梅塔 (Meta) 却没有承担任何后果
author: speckx
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Also here's a cool unrelated photo of a chipmunk

Look at this little guy. They don't know what an AI model is and they're so much better offIt’s nothing short of an indictment of our society at large that Aaron Swartz, one of the co-creators of the RSS protocol (among many other things) was effectively assasinated by our legal system for “illegally” downloading about 70 gigabytes of academic articles from JSTOR - charged so excessively to be made an example of (we're talking 35 years in prison, $1million USD fine, and asset forfeiture) to the point where he felt the need to take his own life rather than deal with the court circus and impending financial ruin - while Facebook (oh I’m sorry Meta) has torrented 80 TERABYTES of books to train their AI models with virtually no consequences other than a court case they will most likely get some sort of financial slap on the wrist for while their AI models continue to print them money. Swartz' use case was the dissemination and archival of knowledge; Meta's use case is powering up their proprietary plagiarism code that cooks the environment while giving CEO's psychosis and making one of the world's richest people even richer. I never met Aaron but I get mad on his behalf so often and I don't know what to do with it other than get more radicalized. Maybe that's for the best.
Anyway, here's your end-of-post cat photo. Her name is Lilith and she's wondering why we don't do something about all these tech billionares.

comments.author: milkytron
comments.textRawHtml:
The part that still bothers me so much about the US vs Swartz case is that JSTOR didn't pursue civil litigation against Aaron. It was the US government that pursued him.

There was little for the government to lose in the case. In a case vs Meta, at the scale it has reached, it could have wide ranging economic implications limiting the investment in AI, which the US is absolutely not willing to pursue at this point in time (or possibly ever).

Basically, being a rich public company provides legal advantages when the US government has similar goals.

The whole thing is incredibly sad and exposes the hypocrisy of the US court system and government as a whole.

RIP Aaron.
comments.textZhHtml:
US vs Swartz 案中最让我困扰的是 JSTOR 没有对 Aaron 提起民事诉讼。追捕他的是美国政府。

政府在此案中几乎没有什么损失。在针对 Meta 的案件中，就其规模而言，它可能会产生广泛的经济影响，限制对人工智能的投资，而美国目前（或可能永远）绝对不愿意追求人工智能。

基本上，当美国政府有类似的目标时，成为一家富有的上市公司会提供法律优势。

整件事令人难以置信的悲伤，暴露了美国法院系统和整个政府的虚伪。

安息吧。亚伦。

children.author: arionhardison
children.textRawHtml:
Maybe the real issue is selective outrage about legal injustice. I totally agree that this was wrong and he should not have been prosecuted but a large part of the effort that dealt this injustice to him was facilitated by the fact that the vast majority of people willfully turn a blind eye when the same thing or worse happens to people are not of their ilk. If we were to finally stand up and say that justice for all means justice for ALL; we might be able to prevent the next Aaron Swartz.

Edit: As someone that has done both state and fed time, the thing that makes me the saddest here is that the charges would have been drastically reduced if not dismissed and his appeals would have had a high probability of success. They use this "scare tatic" so much and I understand why it works; the possibility of facing those years is terrifying. I don't mean that in any demeaning manner, 25/26 and never having done time I cannot imagine how terrified he must have been.

Edit: I would also like to bring attention to the fact that M. Zuckerberg aggressively pursues these types of cases against people for doing far less than he has done.
children.textZhHtml:
也许真正的问题是对法律不公正的选择性愤怒。 我完全同意这是错误的，他不应该被起诉，但对他造成这种不公正的很大一部分努力是由于这样一个事实：当同样的事情或更糟糕的事情发生在非同类人身上时，绝大多数人故意视而不见。如果我们最终站起来说，为所有人伸张正义就意味着为所有人伸张正义；我们也许能够阻止下一个亚伦·斯沃茨。

编辑：作为一个既做过州政府又做过联邦调查局工作的人，最让我难过的是，如果不被驳回，指控将会大幅减少，而且他的上诉很有可能成功。 他们经常使用这种“恐吓策略”，我明白为什么它会起作用；面对那些年的可能性是可怕的。 我并不是说以任何贬低的方式，25/26并且从未完成过时间，我无法想象他一定有多害怕。

编辑：我还想提请注意这样一个事实：扎克伯格先生积极追究此类案件，针对那些做得远远少于他的人。

children.author: giantg2
children.textRawHtml:
"Maybe the real issue is selective outrage about legal injustice."

The real issue is selective enforcement of the law. If it applied equally to everyone, then more people would be outraged as it affected them.
children.textZhHtml:
“也许真正的问题是对法律不公正的选择性愤怒。”

真正的问题是选择性地执行法律。如果它同样适用于每个人，那么更多的人会因为它影响到他们而感到愤怒。

children.author: AnthonyMouse
children.textRawHtml:
> If it applied equally to everyone, then more people would be outraged as it affected them.

In order to do this you need to have laws that are designed to be reasonable for people to actually follow instead of laws that are designed to allow prosecutors to find a violation whenever they want to.

Actually enforcing them would create pressure to do that, but it would also create pressure to go back to selective enforcement when powerful people object to being subjected to the unreasonableness of existing laws.

A better solution might be to make a showing of selective enforcement a means to strike down a law. If you can show that someone else was doing the same thing without being charged then the prosecution either has to charge them too or that law is struck down and no one can be charged with it anymore.

Then instead of the incentive not to charge powerful people creating pressure for selective enforcement, the same incentive creates pressure to strike down the laws that can't reasonably be uniformly enforced.
children.textZhHtml:
> 如果它平等地适用于每个人，那么更多的人会因为它影响到他们而感到愤怒。

为了做到这一点，你需要制定合理的法律，让人们真正遵守，而不是旨在允许检察官随时发现违规行为的法律。

实际上执行这些法律会产生这样做的压力，但当有权势的人反对受到约束时，也会产生返回选择性执法的压力。现有法律的不合理性。

更好的解决方案可能是将选择性执法的表现作为废除法律的手段。如果你能证明其他人在没有受到指控的情况下做了同样的事情，那么检方要么必须对他们也提出指控，要么法律被废除，没有人可以再被指控。

然后，不是激励不起诉有权势的人，为选择性执法创造压力，同样的激励会产生压力，废除那些无法合理统一执行的法律。

children.author: anthonyrstevens
children.textRawHtml:
>> A better solution might be to make a showing of selective enforcement a means to strike down a law. If you can show that someone else was doing the same thing without being charged then the prosecution either has to charge them too or that law is repealed and no one can be charged with it anymore.

This is very interesting. I suspect there are a lot of unintended consequences that might follow.
children.textZhHtml:
>> 更好的解决方案可能是将选择性执法的表现作为废除法律的手段。如果你能证明其他人在没有受到指控的情况下做了同样的事情，那么检方要么也必须对他们提出指控，要么法律被废除，没有人可以再受到指控。

这非常有趣。我怀疑可能会产生很多意想不到的后果。

This is basically asking for discovery of another case when you are being suing for one case.

I think the US court system is famous for being slow. Not sure if anyone wants to make it go even slower.

我认为美国法院系统以缓慢着称。不确定是否有人想让它变得更慢。

children.textRawHtml:
TBTF is not a thing. It's all in your mind. Evergrande and Country Garden would've been classified TBTF in the minds of many USians, yet they failed.

下面 AnthonyMouse 的死评论已经指出，即使在你的情况下，也与现状没有任何区别。它已经死了，散发着人造草皮的臭味，这太疯狂了，因为它没有什么值得标记的。

children.author: john01dav
children.textRawHtml:
Ideally what would happen is the corporation starts having enforcement action against it and then its leadership is forced out to rescue said corporation from failing.

This certainly seems better than just making TBTF (which I assume means too big to fail) entities be above the law.
children.textZhHtml:
理想情况下，公司开始对其采取执法行动，然后其领导层被迫下台，以挽救该公司免于破产。

这显然比仅仅让 TBTF（我认为这意味着太大而不能倒闭）实体凌驾于法律之上要好。

children.author: AnthonyMouse
children.textRawHtml:
Isn't that the other way around? The law already can't be enforced against the TBTF corporation, so what do they care if it stays on the books? But now you can't enforce it against someone else or they can point to you not enforcing it against them.

Except that's the point. The government would now have to do that or they lose the law. If it's a good law then they don't want to lose it, but if it's a good law then they should be enforcing it against them.

And, of course, the correct way to deal with this is to break the TBTF corporations into many smaller pieces so that stops being a problem.
children.textZhHtml:
这不是相反吗？该法律已经无法针对 TBTF 公司执行，那么如果该法律保留在账本上，他们又关心什么呢？但现在你不能对其他人强制执行它，或者他们可以指出你没有对他们强制执行它。

但这就是重点。政府现在必须这样做，否则他们就会失去法律。如果这是一部好法律，那么他们不想失去它，但如果这是一部好法律，那么他们应该对他们执行它。

当然，处理这个问题的正确方法是将 TBTF 公司分解成许多更小的部分，这样就不再是一个问题。

children.author: JackFr
children.textRawHtml:
Congress (and state legislatures) pass laws, but don’t necessarily authorize the resources to prosecute all offenders, so prosecutors are given some latitude who to target.

IANAL, but my understanding is this: Malicious prosecution is a defense. Selective enforcement is not. The difference is for judges and juries to decide.
children.textZhHtml:
国会（和州立法机构）通过法律，但不一定授权资源起诉所有罪犯，因此检察官有一定的自由度来针对谁。

IANAL，但我的理解是：恶意起诉是一种辩护。选择性执法则不然。区别在于法官和陪审团来决定。

children.author: giantg2
children.textRawHtml:
"If you can show that someone else was doing the same thing without being charged"

It's unlikely people would have enough evidence of high enough quality to make that case. The prosecution will just say the evidence isn't enough.
children.textZhHtml:
“如果你能证明其他人也在做同样的事情而没有受到指控”

人们不太可能有足够高质量的证据来证明这一点。检方只会说证据不足。

children.author: AnthonyMouse
children.textRawHtml:
The prosecution can say whatever they want, but the worst of the existing laws are the one that are pretty easy to prove, and it's the court rather than the prosecution who makes the decision.

You'll also get some nice incentives where the government will be arguing that a particular behavior is not a violation of the law so they don't have to charge someone they don't want to, which in turn leaves you with that precedent if the judge agrees with them and then they want to charge someone else for doing that later.
children.textZhHtml:
检方可以说任何他们想说的话，但现有法律中最糟糕的部分是很容易证明的，而且是法院而不是检方做出决定。

你还会得到一些很好的激励，政府会辩称某种特定行为不违反法律，这样他们就不必起诉他们不想起诉的人，这反过来又给你留下了这样的先例，如果法官同意他们的观点，然后他们想向其他人收取稍后这样做的费用。

children.author: skinfaxi
children.textRawHtml: I think part of the balance is that law requires discretion because humans are not good at making deny lists which the law boils down to.
children.textZhHtml: 我认为平衡的一部分是法律要求自由裁量权，因为人类不擅长制定法律归结为的拒绝名单。

children.author: AnthonyMouse
children.textRawHtml: That's just conceding that you don't actually want to have laws and really only want to punish people when you don't like them.
children.textZhHtml: 这只是承认您实际上并不想要法律，而只是想在您不喜欢的人时惩罚他们。
